comments.author: @xp2510
comments.text:
90% of content posted does not equal 90% of content consumed. If content is perceived as "slop", people do not and will not read it. Generating "slop" is basically a spamming strategy - catching the most uncritical suckers because it's so cheap to produce. In reality, people will continue to gravitate to quality human content or, at some point, quality AI content. "Quality" being the operative word.

Model collapse continues to be a perennial bogeyman that never actually makes a dent in real world AI models. Modern LLMs are already good enough that they can identify "slop"-like content if you send them to a link. Presumably they'll be able to filter out their own training data until such point that "AI" becomes synonymous with better, not worse quality.

Will be end up consuming much of our media through ChatGPT or whatever other AI as a portal to the world? Possibly.
